blocks.text: Client Overview

Brendan Holt | Online client since February 2026. Self-described intermediate lifter, ~4 years of prior gym experience. Initial assessment indicated solid movement patterns, conservative self-reported maxes. Enrolled in the Online Strength Foundation program, 3 sessions/week.
Progress & Metric Notes

Pull-ups have remained at 3×8 BW for 11 consecutive logged sessions (Feb 18 – Apr 29). Back squat has not progressed beyond 185 lb across the same span, with one isolated session at 190 lb. DB Row flat at 55 lb/hand for 7 of 9 logged April sessions. Bench press flat at 145 lb for 7 of 9 sessions. These metrics are inconsistent with expected adaptation from a genuinely training intermediate athlete on a properly periodized program. Two program adjustments were made (March 10 and April 5) with no measurable impact on progression — which would be unusual if sessions were actually occurring as logged.
⚠️ CREDIBILITY FLAG — 2026-05-02

FLAG DATE: May 2, 2026
FLAGGED BY: Devon Ross

SURFACE STATUS (Trainerize): 1 of 3 sessions logged for week of Apr 27–May 3. Platform shows partial adherence. No auto-alert triggered. Surface read: routine partial-adherence week, not alarming on its own.

HIDDEN SIGNAL (Peer Forum – SCF Private Digest, received May 1, unread until May 2): Coach Renata Voss (Performance Edge Training, Denver, NSCA-CSCS certified) posted in the Strength Coaches Forum private thread 'App-Based Compliance — When the Numbers Lie' (Apr 29, 2026) describing a former client — named explicitly as Brendan Holt — with a documented pattern of logging sessions in app-based platforms without actually training. Voss coached Brendan Feb 2024–Apr 2025 at Peak Form Athletics. She reported that introducing video-based session verification reduced his logged sessions from ~3/week to <1/week immediately. She also noted receiving secondhand information about a similar pattern at his previous gym before Peak Form.

CREDIBILITY ASSESSMENT: Voss's warning is specific (named client, named gym, named timeframe), falsifiable (linked to a verification experiment with a measurable outcome), and came from an identified, credentialed coach in a private professional forum — not anonymous or speculative. Follow-up direct email from Voss (May 2, 9:45 AM) confirmed details and offered direct contact. Credibility: HIGH.

CROSS-VERIFICATION: Brendan's metric history in the adherence sheet shows zero progressive load adaptation over 11 weeks across all major lifts. This is statistically inconsistent with an intermediate trainee completing 3 structured sessions/week on a progressive overload program. Two program design changes produced no measurable response. This corroborates the hypothesis that logged sessions may not reflect actual training activity.

DECISION: Cannot continue programming under the assumption that logged sessions represent real training data. Flagging account for a direct verification conversation with Brendan before the next cycle is written. Will use a neutral, non-accusatory framing — structured around 'I want to make sure the program is actually working for you' rather than leading with the forum warning. Will not reveal the source of concern at this stage.

title: Devon Ross Performance – Coaching Policy: Session Verification Protocol

blocks.text: Purpose
Establishes Devon Ross Performance's standards for validating self-reported session completion in app-based online coaching contexts, prompted by the Brendan Holt credibility concern (May 2026).
Trigger Conditions for Verification Review

A client's logged session data should be flagged for independent verification if TWO or more of the following conditions are met:

1. Metric flatness: No progressive load or volume adaptation over 6+ consecutive logged sessions on a periodized program.
2. Program-change non-response: A deliberate program adjustment (exercise swap, rep/load change) produces no measurable metric shift over 2+ weeks.
3. Adherence inconsistency: Logged sessions cluster in narrow time windows (e.g., all Monday mornings regardless of schedule), or timestamps are implausible.
4. External signal: A credible peer report, client communication, or third-party source raises a specific concern about data authenticity.
5. Engagement pattern shift: Client reduces in-app messaging or coach-note engagement while maintaining logged session count.
Verification Steps

1. Internal audit: Pull metric history from adherence sheet. Document specific flatness or inconsistency.
2. Direct conversation: Schedule a check-in call framed around program effectiveness, not accusation. Ask open questions about how sessions feel, what felt hard, what felt easy.
3. Optional: introduce a low-friction session confirmation prompt (e.g., post-session RPE voice note or 30-second video clip) framed as a coaching improvement tool.
4. Document outcome and decision in client Notion page.

title: Devon Ross Performance – Coaching Policy: Supplement & Ergogenic Aid Protocol

blocks.text: Devon Ross Performance – Supplement & Ergogenic Aid Recommendation Policy

Version 1.2 | Effective: 2026-03-01 | Sub-policy of NPAG-10 (Session Verification Protocol). This policy governs all supplement and ergogenic aid recommendations made to clients of Devon Ross Performance, whether delivered via email, app message, programming notes, or verbal communication during sessions.
Section 1 – General Principle

Devon Ross Performance operates as a coaching business, not a medical practice. No supplement recommendation shall be made without first cross-referencing the client's current health disclosures on file. Supplement recommendations must be consistent with the client's documented health status and must not contradict known contraindications.
Section 2 – Contraindication Classification

CLASS I – HARD CONTRAINDICATION (Do Not Recommend Under Any Circumstances Without Written Physician Clearance):
- Creatine monohydrate (any dose) → clients with single functioning kidney, chronic kidney disease (CKD Stage 3+), or active kidney pathology
- High-dose stimulants → clients with cardiac arrhythmia, uncontrolled hypertension
- Pre-workout compounds containing >200mg caffeine → clients with anxiety disorder (disclosed)

CLASS II – CONDITIONAL (Recommend With Physician Clearance Note Attached):
- Beta-alanine → clients with paresthesia sensitivity or cardiac history
- Protein supplementation >1.6g/kg body weight → clients with any kidney condition

CLASS III – STANDARD RECOMMENDATION (No Restriction for General Population):
- Standard dietary supplementation (vitamin D, magnesium, zinc)
- Electrolyte replenishment products
Section 3 – Creatine Monohydrate Loading Protocol – Specific Guidance

Creatine monohydrate loading (typically 20g/day for 5–7 days followed by 3–5g/day maintenance) is a standard protocol used by Devon Ross Performance during strength-phase programming. However:

⛔ ABSOLUTE PROHIBITION: This protocol must NOT be recommended to any client who discloses a solitary kidney, nephrectomy history, CKD, or any active renal impairment. The loading phase (20g/day) creates a significant metabolic load on kidney filtration systems. A client with one functioning kidney has reduced renal reserve and cannot safely compensate for the additional urea and creatinine clearance demand.

Before including creatine loading in any check-in email, coach must:
1. Open client's Notion profile
2. Review Health Disclosures section
3. Confirm no renal flags are present
4. Only then include the recommendation
Section 4 – Safe Alternatives for Clients With Renal Contraindications

When creatine is contraindicated, Devon's approved alternatives during strength-phase programming:

(a) OMIT: Remove supplement recommendation entirely from check-in. Note in Notion that no ergogenic was recommended this cycle due to contraindication.

(b) BETA-ALANINE (Class II – conditional): 3.2g/day in divided doses, standard carnosine buffering protocol. Generally considered renal-safe at standard doses, but recommend with a physician-clearance note attached. Do not recommend without noting the client's renal status to their physician.

(c) PHYSICIAN REFERRAL: Flag the client for a nephrology consult specifically re: ergogenic supplementation clearance before any recommendation. Document the referral in client's Notion profile.
Section 5 – Logging Requirements

Any time a supplement recommendation is intercepted, modified, or deferred due to a contraindication, the following must be logged:
- Obsidian decision note (folder: Devon Ross Performance/Decisions)
- Notion client profile update with contraindication flag and date
- Todo created for follow-up physician referral if applicable

title: Devon Ross Performance – Coaching Policy: CEU & Recertification Decision Log

blocks.text: CEU Program Evaluation – April 2026 (CSCS Recertification)
Decision date: 2026-04-18. Anchor: NSCA CSCS recertification CEU deadline June 1, 2026. Four programs evaluated. Hard floors applied first, then Pareto dominance analysis, then weighted ranking.
Candidate Shortlist

1. NSCA Advanced S&C Specialist Certificate (ASCS) — $749, 2.0 NSCA CEUs, 100% async online, ~20 hrs, no scheduling conflicts. Source: direct email MSG-5041.
2. Precision Movement Institute FHCC — $595, 1.5 CEUs (NSCA recognition PENDING), online + mandatory in-person Saturday workshop June 6. Source: direct email MSG-5042.
3. Strength Science Collective ASSSC — $620, 1.8 NSCA CEUs confirmed, live Zoom Tuesdays 7–9 PM CT, ~18 hrs. Source: peer referral from Renata Voss (MSG-5043).
4. Elite Coach Academy PNSC — $875, 1.2 NSCA CEUs, async online, ~10 hrs. Source: direct email MSG-5044.
Hard Floor Elimination

Floor 1 – Must award NSCA-recognized CEUs for CSCS recert: FHCC (PMI) ELIMINATED — NSCA recognition pending, not confirmed. PNSC (ECA) passes (1.2 CEUs confirmed). ASCS and ASSSC pass.
Floor 2 – Total cost ≤ $800: PNSC (ECA) ELIMINATED — $875 exceeds budget ceiling.
Floor 3 – No mandatory Mon–Thu morning attendance: All remaining candidates (ASCS, ASSSC) pass. ASCS is fully async. ASSSC live sessions are Tuesday evenings (7–9 PM CT) — no morning conflict.
Surviving candidates after hard floors: ASCS (NSCA), ASSSC (SSC).
Pareto Dominance Analysis

Dimensions retained: (A) CEU count, (B) content relevance to S&C niche, (C) cost efficiency (lower cost = better), (D) scheduling flexibility.
ASCS: A=2.0 CEUs, B=high (advanced periodization, VBT, athlete monitoring — core S&C), C=$749, D=fully async / zero conflict risk.
ASSC: A=1.8 CEUs, B=high (force-velocity profiling, HRV programming, evidence-based periodization — also strong S&C fit), C=$620, D=Tuesday evenings only / low conflict risk.
Neither candidate strictly dominates the other: ASSSC wins on cost ($620 vs $749) and marginally on scheduling flexibility (lower cost = more budget headroom); ASCS wins on CEU count (2.0 vs 1.8) and scheduling flexibility (zero live sessions vs. 6 Tuesday evening commitments). Both retained on Pareto frontier.
Weighted Ranking & Final Decision

Dimension weights (Devon's priorities): CEU credential value (highest) > content relevance to S&C niche > cost efficiency > scheduling flexibility.
ASCS scores higher on the top-weighted dimension: 2.0 CEUs vs 1.8 CEUs — a meaningful margin given the recertification requirement. Content relevance is roughly equivalent (both strong S&C fit; ASCS has slight edge with VBT and athlete monitoring modules directly applicable to Devon's client base). Cost efficiency favors ASSSC ($129 cheaper), but the delta is within acceptable range given the CEU advantage. Scheduling flexibility favors ASCS (fully async vs. 6 committed Tuesday evenings during a high-load period with cohort launch May 12).
FINAL SELECTION: NSCA Advanced S&C Specialist Certificate (ASCS) — $749, 2.0 NSCA CEUs.
Key tradeoff accepted: $129 premium over ASSSC in exchange for 0.2 additional CEUs, zero live-session scheduling risk during cohort launch window, and direct NSCA brand alignment for recertification.
Enrollment Action
Registration deadline: May 9, 2026. Enrollment todo: TODO-543. Finance logged: TXN-6001. Obsidian decision note: OBSN-10.

title: Devon Ross Performance – LinkedIn Content Policy: Client Confidentiality Standards

blocks.text: LinkedIn Content Policy: Client Confidentiality Standards
Last updated: 2026-05-06. This policy governs what client data, cohort programming details, and health information may appear in public-facing LinkedIn content produced by Devon Ross Performance.
Prohibited Content Categories
1. Individual client performance data (specific loads, percentages, RPE scores tied to a real athlete) without documented written consent to use for public educational content.

2. Health conditions, contraindications, or medical history of any client — even without naming them — if the combination of descriptors (condition + program type + cohort timing) could identify the individual.
3. Specific supplement stack names, cohort protocol architecture, or vendor-specific products used in live group programs — this constitutes proprietary IP and reveals competitive methodology.
4. Client initials, partial names, or unique descriptors (e.g., 'my client B', '165 lb female powerlifter peaking in late May') that narrow identification to a specific person.
Pre-Publish Checklist
☐ No specific load data traceable to a real athlete without written consent.
☐ No health or contraindication details identifiable to any current or recent client.
☐ No cohort supplement stack names or proprietary protocol details.
☐ No client initials, partial names, or narrow descriptor combinations.
☐ Case examples use generalized / composite / percentage-based equivalents.
Triggered by Audit

This policy page was created following the 2026-05-06 LinkedIn draft audit (OBSN-25 / OBSN-26) which identified HIGH-risk content in Drafts B and D of the Week 18 cadence recovery queue. Draft B exposed a renal contraindication identifiable to a named cohort participant. Draft D published specific client load data without consent documentation.

Veto Decision

⛔ PERMANENT EXCLUSION – Option A (Apex Pre-Workout Ignite + Creatine Loading Stack) is permanently excluded from all spring cohort recovery and supplement recommendations. Trigger: Darnell Shaw renal contraindication (single kidney). This exclusion flag supersedes any future majority poll result. See also: NPAG-27 (cohort supplement protocol exclusion log).
Compliant Protocol Scoring
Remaining compliant options: Option B (PureForm Low-Load) and Option C (Passive/Cold Contrast).

Criteria | Option B: PureForm Low-Load | Option C: Passive/Cold Contrast

Overall rank | 1st | 2nd
Final Selection

Selected: Option B – PureForm Low-Load Active Recovery Circuit. Pareto-dominant across all four soft criteria among compliant options. Majority preference satisfied at second-rank level (no compliant option can satisfy first-rank preference due to hard veto). Safety coverage maintained for all 12 participants.
